["On the 20 February 2013 Independent Oil & Resources ASA has forwarded following letter to the Company's shareholders :Dear shareholder in Independent Oil & Resources ASACOMPULSORY ACQUISITION OF SMALL SHAREHOLDINGS.Independent Oil & Resources ASA (\"the company\") set forth on the 5th August 2011 a voluntary offer to shareholders who owned less than 10,000 shares. The reason for the offer was to reduce costs associated with managing the company's shareholder base.The company received many acceptances, but not from all who received the offer. In was therefore announced in the offer letter that the company would submit an application to the Ministry of Trade and Industry for compulsory redemption of shares that have a market capitalization of less than NOK 500, which the Public Companies Act § 4-24 subsection 2 allows for.In a letter dated 6th February 2013, the Ministry of Trade and Industry gives the company permission to conduct such a forced redemption.Permission from the Ministry of Trade and Industry\"The Ministry of Trade and Industry has requested Independent Oil & Resources ASA to include the following text in this letter, ref The Public Administration Act of 10 February 1967 §§ 2-27:The Ministry of Trade and Industry has, in accordance with The Public Companies Act of 13 June 1997 No. 45 § 4-24, second paragraph, royal decree of 17 July 1998 No. 619,given Independent Oil & Resources ASA permission for a compulsory acquisition of the shareswhich was comprised in the company's voluntary offer of redemption of 5 August 2011, ie thoseincluded in a portfolio of shares of NOK 500 or less, but which are not acquiredas a result of acceptance of the offer. The permission does not include shares held by shareholderswho following the offer have acquired shares above the redemption limit.The Ministry has in its ruling focused on the company's costs as a result of a substantial number of small shareholdings, and that these are not proportionate to the shares' value for those shareholders covered by the permission to compulsory redemption.Those of the company's shareholders who are affected by the decision, may appeal the decisionpursuant to the Act of 10 February 1967 on the procedure in administrative cases (The Public Administration Act). The appeal deadline is three weeks. The deadline commences from the date this letter is received. The appeal must, in order to be timely, be presented or sent no later than the last day of the deadline. Any complaints can be sent to The Ministry of Trade and Industry, PO Box 8014 Dep, 0030 Oslo. A complaint can request that the implementation of this resolution be postponed until the appeal is settled. Affected shareholders also have the right of access to documents at the Ministry, ref The Public Administration Act § 18, cf § 19 \"Decision on compulsory acquisition and redemption price.On 19th February 2013, the board decided to carry out such a compulsory acquisition in accordance with the permission from the Ministry of Trade and Industry.Price on the shares to be redeemed is set to NOK 0.10/share. The price is the same as was announced in the letter of 5th August 2011, and is the same as the price in the latest rights issue in August 2011. The shares have generally been traded at prices below this level since August 2011. The compulsory acquisition will include approximately 5.500 shareholders, or a total of 2.6% of issued shareholdings.Shareholders whose shares are redeemed must direct any objections regarding the offer in writing to Independent Oil & Resources ASA, Hopsnesveien 127, 5232 Paradis, within 20. April 2013. If objections are not received by this deadline, the shareholder is deemed to have accepted the offered redemption price.The redemption amount will be paid on or about 18th March 2013. The redemption amount will be transferred to the shareholders' bank accounts registered in the Norwegian CSD. If the account is not registered in the Norwegian CSD, the payment to shareholders in Norway will be sent by bank transfer and by cheque to shareholders outside Norway. Shareholders will not be charged with transaction costs in connection with the compulsory acquisition. Shareholders who oppose the offered redemption price will, in the absence of an amicable settlement, be determined by judicial discretion in accordance with the Public Companies Act § 4-25.For further information, please contact the writer. Telephone +4740400430.Yours sincerelyIndependent Oil & Resources ASAJan Egil MoeChairman(sign.)"]

["Independent Oil & Resources ASA har den 20. februar 2013 sendt følgende brev til sine aksjonærer :Kjære aksjonær i Independent Oil & Resources ASA TVANGSINNLØSNING AV SMÅ AKSJEPOSTER.Independent Oil & Resources ASA (\"selskapet\") fremsatte den 5. august 2011 et frivillig tilbud til de aksjonærer som eide færre enn 10.000 aksjer i selskapet. Bakgrunnen for tilbudet var å redusere kostnadene forbundet med administrasjon av selskapets aksjonærbase.Selskapet mottok mange aksepter, men på langt nær fra samtlige som mottok tilbudet. I tilbudsbrevet ble det derfor meddelt at selskapet ville oversende søknad til Nærings- og handelsdepartementet om tvungen innløsning av aksjeposter som har en markedsverdi som er lavere enn kr. 500, slik allmennaksjeloven § 4-24.2 ledd gir adgang til. I brev datert 6. februar 2013 gir Nærings- og handelsdepartementet selskapet tillatelse til å gjennomføre en slik tvangsinnløsing.Tillatelse fra Nærings- og handelsdepartementet Nærings- og handelsdepartementet har bedt Independent Oil & Resources ASA om å innta følgende tekst i dette brevet, jf. forvaltningsloven av 10. februar 1967 §§ 2-.27:Nærings- og handelsdepartementet har i henhold til lov 13. Juni 1997 nr. 45 om allmennaksjeselskaper § 4-24 annet ledd, jf. kongelig resolusjon av 17. Juli 1998 nr. 619, gitt Independent Oil & Resources ASA tillatelse om tvungen overtakelse av de aksjene som var omfattet av selskapets frivillige tilbud om innløsning av 5. August 2011, dvs. de som inngikk i en aksjebeholdning på 500 kroner eller mindre, men som ikke er ervervet som følge av aksept av tilbudet. Tillatelsen omfatter ikke aksjer eid av aksjeeiere som etter fremsettelsen av det frivillige tilbudet har kjøpt seg opp til over innløsningsgrensen.Departementet har i sin avgjørelse lagt vekt på selskapets kostnader som følge av at aksjene er spredt på mange og svært små aksjeposter ikke står i rimelig forhold til aksjenes verdi for de aksjeeiere som omfattes av tillatelsen til tvangsinnløsning.De av selskapets aksjeeiere som blir berørt av vedtaket kan påklage vedtaket etter reglene i lov av 10. februar 1967 om behandlingsmåten i forvaltningssaker (forvaltningsloven.) Klagefristen er tre uker. Fristen begynner å løpe fra det tidspunkt dette brevet er mottatt. Klagen må, for å være rettidig, være fremsatt eller sendt senest den dagen fristen går ut. Eventuelle klager kan sendes til Nærings- og handelsdepartmentet, Postboks 8014 Dep, 0030 Oslo. Ved klage kan det bes om at gjennomføringen av dette vedtaket utsettes til klagesaken er avgjort. Berørte aksjeeiere har også rett til dokumentinnsyn hos departementet etter forvaltningsloven § 18, jf. § 19.\"Beslutning om tvangsinnløsning og innløsningspris.Selskapet har i styremøte 19. februar 2013 besluttet å gjennomføre tvangsinnløsningen iht. tillatelsen fra Nærings- og handelsdepartementet.Pris på aksjene som tvangsinnløses er satt til kr. 0.10/aksje. Prisen er den samme som ble meddelt i brev av 5. august 2011, og tilsvarer kursen i siste tegningsrettsemisjon i august 2011. Aksjene har i stor grad vært omsatt til kurser under dette nivået siden august 2011. Tvangsinnløsningen omfatter ca. 5.500 aksjonærer, og utgjør ca.2.6% av utestående aksjer.Aksjonærer som tvangsinnløses må rette eventuelle innsigelser mot tilbudet om innløsningssum skriftlig til Independent Oil & Resources ASA, Hopsnesveien 127, 5232 Paradis, innen 20. april 2013. Dersom innsigelser ikke er mottatt innen denne fristen anses aksjonæren å hå akseptert den tilbudte innløsningssummen.Innløsningssummen vil utbetales ca. 18 mars 2013. Innløsningssummen vil bli overført til aksjonærenes bankkonti som registrert i VPS. Hvis konto ikke er registrert i VPS, vil utbetalingen til aksjonær i Norge sendes med bankgiro og med sjekk til aksjonærer utenfor Norge. Aksjonærene vil ikke bli belastet med transaksjonskostnader i forbindelse med tvangsinnløsningen. Aksjonærer som motsetter seg den tilbudte løsningssum, vil i mangel av minnelig overenskomst fastsettes ved rettslig skjønn i henhold til allmennaksjeloven § 4-25.For ytterligere informasjon, vennligst kontakt undertegnede. Telefon 40400430.Med vennlig hilsenIndependent Oil & Resources ASAJan Egil MoeStyreformann(sign.)"]

["FORELØPIG REGNSKAP PR. 31.12.04Sammendrag:Etter forslag fra morselskapet, DNO ASA, besluttet ekstraordinær generalforsamling i Independent Oil Tools AS 16. november 2004 å omdanne selskapet til allmennaksjeselskap. DNO ASA hadde i forkant av omdannelsen vedtatt å distribuere sine Independent Oil Tools ASA (IOT) aksjer til DNOs aksjeeiere som naturalutbytte. I forbindelse med denne prosessen, ble selskapets aksjekapital vedtatt forhøyet fra NOK 1.385.000 til NOK 1.413.839 på den ekstraordinære generalforsamlingen i Independent Oil Tools AS 16. november 2004.I forbindelse med at DNO ASA vedtok å utdele sine aksjer i Independent Oil Tools ASA som naturalutbytte til DNO-aksjonærene, vedtok styret i Independent Oil Tools ASA å legge til rette for handel av aksjene på NOTC-listen. Slik handel har funnet sted siden 17. desember 2004. Selskapets hovedvirksomhet er rettet mot utleie av bore- og testerør med tilhørende utstyr, samt service og vedlikehold relatert til dette. Virksomheten er lokalisert i Stavanger og aktiviteten retter seg hovedsakelig mot norsk kontinentalsokkel, men er også økende internasjonalt. I tillegg er selskapet hovedaksjonær i det børsnoterte riggselskapet Petrolia Drilling ASA. Selskapet deltok i en refinansiering av Petrolia Drilling ASA (PDR) i 2004 og har i denne forbindelse gitt henstand med betaling av forfalt og fremtidig leie under finansielle leieavtaler, totalt NOK 64.4 mill. Som kompensasjon for dette har selskapet mottatt 128.8 mill tegningsretter i PDR til en tegningskurs på NOK 0.55 pr aksje. I tillegg har selskapet 50 millioner aksjer i PDR anskaffet gjennom emisjon og konvertering av obligasjonslån.Selskapet har til hensikt å utvide sin investeringsvirksomhet, primært innenfor offshoresegmenter som kan styrke selskapets utleievirksomhet, herunder ytterligere rigginvesteringer. Det vises for øvrig til Information Memorandum datert 24. november 2004 for ytterligere beskrivelse av selskapets strategi (dokumentet er tilgjengelig på selskapets hjemmeside: www.independent.no).Driften i 2004 har vært preget av lav aktivitet på kontinentalsokkelen, blant annet på grunn av lav leteborings-aktivitet samt den langvarige offshore-konflikten høsten 2004."]

["Styret i Independent Oil Tools ASA (IOT) har den 14. januar 2005 vedtatt å erverve 1.636.923 aksjer i Petrojack AS til kurs NOK 6,50 per aksje. IOT vil etter ervervet ha en eierandel tilsvarende 4,2% i Petrojack. Som betaling for aksjene i Petrojack har IOT utstedt 5.600.000 aksjer i IOT, til kurs NOK 1,90 per aksje, gjennom en rettet emisjon, stor NOK 10.640.000, mot selger av Petrojack-aksjene. Den rettede emisjonen er gjennomført på basis av styrefullmakt gitt av generalforsamlingen i IOT den 16. november 2004. Tegneren av IOT-aksjene (Net AS), har etter sin tegning i den rettede emisjonen en eierandel i IOT tilsvarende 9,0%.Investeringen i Petrojack er i tråd med IOTs strategi om å øke sin eksponering mot rigg-segmentet i et stigende riggmarked. I forbindelse med den rettede emisjonen vil IOTs aksjekapital øke med NOK 140.000, fra NOK 1.413.839, til NOK 1.553.839. Antall aksjer vil øke fra 56.553.560 til 62.153.560, hver pålydende NOK 0,025. IOT vil sende melding når ny firmaattest foreligger."]

["", "Stan Magidson, KC, LLM, ICD.D Office of the Chair and Executive Officer Mr. Magidson is Chair and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Alberta Securities Commission and possesses extensive experience in corporate governance and securities law and regulation. Before joining the ASC in July 2016, he was President, CEO and director of the Institute of Corporate Directors and Chair of the Global Network of Director Institutes. Prior, Mr. Magidson was a partner for 21 years with a national law firm in the business law group where he advised corporate issuers, investors, financial intermediaries and boards of directors across the country on securities law, corporate finance, mergers and acquisitions and corporate governance matters. Mr. Magidson currently serves as Chair of the Canadian Securities Administrators. The CSA, the council of the securities regulators of Canada’s provinces and territories, co-ordinates and harmonizes regulation for the Canadian capital markets. Mr. Magidson also currently serves on the international board of the Weizmann Institute of Science and the Advisory Council of Weizmann Canada. Mr. Magidson holds an LLM in Corporate Law from New York University and an LLB from the University of Ottawa."]

["", "Kari Horn, KC Vice-Chair Ms. Horn was appointed Vice-Chair in May 2018. Prior to her appointment to Vice-Chair Ms. Horn was a Member of the ASC’s senior management team as General Counsel since 2005. In this role, she led the group responsible for providing specialized legal advisory services to the Commission, staff, and market participants. She also assisted in formulation of the Commission’s strategic policy direction and provided research and advice on emerging issues. Before joining the ASC, Ms. Horn practised securities and corporate law as a partner with a Calgary-based boutique law firm and prior to that she was as an associate at a national law firm."]

["", "Deanna Steblyk, KC Vice-Chair Ms. Steblyk was appointed Vice-Chair in March 2026. Prior to her appointment, Ms. Steblyk was Senior Special Counsel to the Vice-Chairs, where she assisted the Vice-Chairs and other Commissioners with their adjudicative and policy-making responsibilities. She first joined the ASC in 2008 as Senior Litigation Counsel in the Enforcement division, prosecuting breaches of Alberta securities laws before the Commission tribunal and the Alberta Provincial Court. Before joining the ASC, she practiced civil litigation primarily at two large international law firms."]

["", "Raymond Crossley, FCPA, FCA, ICD.D Lead Independent Member Mr. Crossley became a Member in April 2018 and serves as Chair of the ASC's Governance Committee. He is a highly experienced financial professional and corporate director with strong management and governance skills. In addition to his role with the ASC, Mr. Crossley currently serves on the board of directors of Obsidian Energy Ltd. Most recently, he was Chief Financial Officer of the Calgary Health Foundation before retiring in 2023. Mr. Crossley previously served as Managing Partner, Western Canada for PwC Canada and was the audit partner on a broad range of public companies primarily in the energy sector. He has served on other corporate and not-for-profit boards and as a member of the ASC’s Financial Review Committee and the Financial Advisory Committee. Mr. Crossley holds the ICD.D designation from the Institute of Corporate Directors and is a member of the Institute of Chartered Professional Accountants of Alberta. He graduated from the University of Western Ontario with a degree in Economics and Political Science."]

["", "Matthew Bootle, FCA Mr. Bootle became a Member in April 2019 and serves on the ASC’s Audit Committee. A retired partner with Ernst & Young LLP, Mr. Bootle has over 30 years of experience as a financial and legal professional. He is a former Director of Accounting Standards and Director of Policy at the TSX Venture Exchange and returns to the ASC where he served as Chief Accountant from 1993 to 1997. Mr. Bootle is a Fellow of the Chartered Professional Accountants of Alberta (CPA Alberta) and received a CPA Alberta Distinguished Service Award in 2012, and a CPA Alberta Lifetime Achievement Award in 2025. He received a Bachelor of Commerce, Bachelor of Laws and Master’s degree in Adult Education from the University of Calgary."]

["", "Gail Harding, KC, ICD.D Ms. Harding became a Member in April 2019 and serves on the ASC’s Human Resources Committee. Ms. Harding has over 30 years of experience as a financial services executive and corporate lawyer. She currently serves as Chair of the Board of Meridian Credit Union and is a former director of Pieridae Energy Limited. Ms. Harding previously served as Senior Vice President, Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary at Canadian Western Bank Financial Group. A prior member of the C.D. Howe Financial Services Research Council, she is a recipient of the Canadian General Counsel Award – Mid-Market Excellence and the Women in Law Leadership Award. Ms. Harding received a Bachelor of Education and a Bachelor of Laws from the University of Alberta, a Master of Laws (specialization in Energy and Infrastructure) from York University and holds the ICD.D designation."]

["", "Evan Hazell, P.Eng. Mr. Hazell became a Member in July 2026 and serves on the ASC’s Governance Committee. He brings a breadth of experience with more than 30 years in the global energy industry, first as a petroleum engineer and later as an investment banker specializing in the oil and gas industry. He served as a managing director at several financial institutions, including HSBC Global Investment Bank and RBC Capital Markets. For the past 15 years, Mr. Hazell has been active as a corporate director with various domestic and international organizations, as well as a range of community organizations. Mr. Hazell holds a Master of Engineering degree from the University of Calgary and a Master of Business Administration from the University of Michigan."]

["", "C. Richard Jones, KC Mr. Jones became a Member in July 2026 and serves on the ASC’s Human Resources Committee. He is a highly accomplished lawyer with more than 30 years of experience and is currently with Brownlee LLP. Previously, he practiced with two national law firms and was a founding partner of a commercial litigation boutique. Throughout his career, he has helped public- and private-sector clients navigate complex regulatory landscapes, manage legal risk and address multifaceted matters. His practice encompasses corporate and commercial law, environmental law, municipal law, and natural resource development. Mr. Jones holds an LLB from the University of Calgary and serves as a Director with the Canadian Bitcoin Consortium."]

["", "Karen Kim, CPA, CA, CFA, ICD.D Ms. Kim became a Member in May 2017 and serves as the Chair of the ASC’s Audit Committee. She possesses over 25 years of experience in capital markets, derivatives, risk management and investments. She has worked in progressively more senior finance roles at Petro-Canada and Suncor Energy. Ms. Kim is also a Public member of the Audit Committee for the City of Calgary. She holds a B.Comm (Accounting) from the University of Calgary, and is a Chartered Professional Accountant and Chartered Financial Analyst. Ms. Kim also holds the ICD.D designation from the Institute of Corporate Directors."]

["", "Doug Mair, ICD.D Mr. Mair became a Member in April 2021 and serves on the ASC’s Human Resources Committee. He has over 35 years of experience in the investment industry and is currently with Richardson Wealth Limited. He has a wide range of experience in virtually every segment of the investment industry. Mr. Mair was a founding member of Richardson Partners Financial Ltd. and served on the board for four years, and has served on numerous boards in a variety of private corporations and not-for-profit organizations. Mr. Mair has been a Fellow of the Canadian Securities Institute for over 20 years and holds the ICD.D designation from the Institute of Corporate Directors. Mr. Mair graduated from Queen’s University with a degree in Economics and History."]

["", "Linda Thomas, ICD.D Ms. Thomas became a Member in July 2026 and serves on the ASC’s Audit Committee. She is a seasoned business executive with more than 30 years of experience across telecommunications, technology and consumer packaged goods. Most recently, she served as Senior Vice-President, Commercial Finance at Shaw/Rogers Communications. Throughout her career, she has held leadership roles spanning numerous disciplines including finance, strategy, transformation, product management, marketing and supply chain, with expertise in finance and audit, and mergers and acquisitions. Ms. Thomas is an experienced corporate director and she currently serves on the board of Big Rock Brewery Inc., where she chairs the Audit Committee and sits on other committees. She is also a Senator and Executive Committee member with the University of Calgary Senate. She holds an Honours Bachelor of Mathematics from the University of Waterloo and the ICD.D designation and has completed executive education through the Institute of Corporate Directors, Harvard Executive Education and The Banff Centre."]

["", "Bryce C. Tingle, KC, LLB, LLM Mr. Tingle became a Member in May 2022 and serves on the ASC’s Governance Committee. He has more than 30 years experience as a corporate finance lawyer, initially in private practice, then as the general counsel of large internationally-focused technology and energy companies. He holds the N. Murray Edwards Chair in Business Law at the University of Calgary and currently serves as the board chair of several private technology and asset management companies. He is one of the four members of the National Special Advisory Group for the Integrated Market Enforcement Team of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. Mr. Tingle has been Director of the Financial Markets Regulation Programme at the University of Calgary’s School of Public Policy, a member of the Ontario Securities Commission’s Exempt Markets Committee and the ASC’s Securities Advisory Committee. He has law degrees from the University of Alberta, Osgoode Hall and Duke University and was twice named one of the University of Calgary’s peak scholars. Mr. Tingle’s academic research focuses on corporate governance and entrepreneurial law."]

["", "Andrea Whyte, KC, LLB Ms. Whyte became a Member in November 2024 and serves as Chair of the ASC’s Human Resources Committee. She has over 25 years of experience as a corporate lawyer with a focus on corporate securities, mergers and acquisitions and corporate governance. In addition to her role with the ASC, Ms. Whyte is currently a senior partner at Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt LLP and serves on the board of directors of Maxim Power Corp. and she is a former director of Westbrick Energy Ltd. Ms. Whyte is also a member of Osler’s national partnership board and a member of Osler’s Audit, Finance & Risk Committee. Ms. Whyte holds a B.Sc. from McGill University and a law degree from the University of Alberta."]
